content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: overtime on the 14:00 peak plus free levers lifts service level to 80.8% for 13:30-15:30, meeting the 80% target for INR 2,835.","why":"The problem is extra calls from the card authorisation gateway outage (P1 opened 12:37), not missing staff. Card_declined calls are running at 2.48x normal, payments calls hit 240 against 108 forecast, and service level fell to 2.9% with 84 abandons. P3 offers overtime to 26 payments agents for 14:00-15:00. It also delays payments breaks by 45 minutes and runs IVR callbacks from 13:30-15:30. From 15:00 it moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments, plays the outage message on payments, and cancels coaching from 15:30-16:00. Predicted results for the window: 80.8% overall (payments 76.7%, general 89.3%) and abandons down to 4.0%. Rest-of-day rises to 89.4%. It is the only option that reaches the target, and it breaks no policy.","trade_offs":["Cost: P3 costs INR 2,835 and uses the remaining overtime budget. P1 is free but only reaches 69.0%, and P2 costs INR 324 but only reaches 74.3%.","Customer impact: abandons fall to 4.0% under P3, against 7.2% with no action, 6.3% under P1 and 5.6% under P2. Payments still sits below target at 76.7%, so the overall target is met mainly through general's 89.3%.","Other queue: moving 3 agents out of general from 15:00 costs it a little. General is predicted at 89.3% under P3 versus 90.1% under P2, still well above target.","Staff: breaks are delayed and coaching is cancelled. Overtime depends on enough of the 26 agents accepting."],"watch":"Track overtime acceptance before 14:00 and payments service level through the peak. If take-up is low, or the gateway outage runs past 15:30 and card_declined volumes stay high, payments will fall short and the plan should be revisited. Escalation is not flagged at this point."}
